backlog.title: Repository Root Resolution (Upward .git Traversal) — §9.8
backlog.description: Make `hack` runnable from any subdirectory of a repository by walking up to the nearest `.git`, `chdir`-ing there, and resolving all default paths (PRD.md, plan/, .hack, .env) against that root. Git is a hard prerequisite: a missing repo aborts at startup. This phase runs FIRST in the bootstrap sequence because the .hack project layers (Phase 2) live at the repo root.

milestones.title: Resolver Engine, Bootstrap Wiring & CLI Override
milestones.description: Implement the upward .git traversal resolver, wire it into main() bootstrap with chdir + INVOCATION_CWD capture, add the --repo-root CLI override, and verify hard-error behavior and child-process inheritance.

tasks.title: Core resolver, bootstrap chdir, and INVOCATION_CWD semantics
tasks.description: Create the resolveRepositoryRoot function with upward .git traversal (dir-or-file detection), wire it into main() after parseCLIArgs() and before configureEnvironment(), capture INVOCATION_CWD, and perform process.chdir(repoRoot).

subtasks.title: resolveRepositoryRoot + bootstrap chdir in main()
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §2.1 and bootstrap-and-reporoot.md. src/index.ts:main() (line 110) currently calls parseCLIArgs() at line 112 then configureEnvironment() at line 128 — there is NO chdir, NO upward traversal, NO INVOCATION_CWD capture. validateRepositoryPath in src/tools/git-mcp.ts:202-213 already uses existsSync (which accepts .git as BOTH dir or file) but only checks the given path (no upward walk). The new resolver mirrors the dir-or-file acceptance pattern.
2. INPUT: None (foundational bootstrap step — this is the first thing that runs after CLI parsing).
3. LOGIC: Create src/utils/repo-root.ts exporting `resolveRepositoryRoot(startDir: string, opts?: { explicit?: string }): { repoRoot: string; invocationCwd: string }`. Algorithm (§9.8.2): beginning at startDir, walk upward; at each directory test whether it contains a child entry `.git` as EITHER a directory (normal clone) OR a file (worktree/submodule gitdir: pointer — §9.8.4). Use statSync or existsSync to detect .git presence (existsSync is true for both dir and file). Stop at the first ancestor with .git (nearest-ancestor wins). If the filesystem root (path.dirname(dir) === dir) is reached without .git, throw a typed error NotARepositoryError carrying the searched-from dir and the --repo-root remediation string. On success, canonicalize via realpathSync(repoRoot). Export class NotARepositoryError extends Error. Wire into src/index.ts:main(): at the very top of main() (before line 112 parseCLIArgs), capture INVOCATION_CWD = process.cwd() in a module-level const. After parseCLIArgs() returns ValidatedCLIArgs (the non-subcommand branch, after line 119) and BEFORE configureEnvironment() (line 128): call resolveRepositoryRoot(INVOCATION_CWD), then process.chdir(repoRoot). Export the resolved repoRoot and INVOCATION_CWD as read-only (small module singleton in repo-root.ts, e.g. getRepoRoot() / getInvocationCwd() accessors). IMPORTANT: --help/--version/usage errors already short-circuit during parseCLIArgs() via Commander's process.exit and must NOT reach the traversal — confirm by placing the traversal AFTER the parseCLIArgs() return.
4. OUTPUT: src/utils/repo-root.ts with resolveRepositoryRoot, NotARepositoryError, getRepoRoot(), getInvocationCwd(); main() updated to traverse + chdir before env config. Consumed by P1.M1.T1.S2 (--repo-root flag) and P2.M1.T1.S2 (.hack loader needs repoRoot).
5. MOCKING: Mock process.cwd(), existsSync/statSync, realpathSync via vitest vi.mock for traversal tests. Use real temp dirs with actual .git dirs for integration tests.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc on resolveRepositoryRoot documenting the dir-or-file .git detection, nearest-ancestor rule, and hard-error contract. Add a bootstrap-ordering comment at the main() insertion site noting 'chdir happens after parseCLIArgs() and before configureEnvironment() per §9.8.3 / §9.7.9'.

subtasks.title: --repo-root <path> flag + explicit-path vs default-path semantics
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §2.2. CLI flags are registered on the root `program` chain in src/cli/index.ts:310-436 (e.g. `.option('-p, --prd <path>', ...)`, line 312). The CLIArgs interface (~line 100) and ValidatedCLIArgs interface (~line 180) define the typed args. parseCLIArgs() returns ValidatedCLIArgs at the end (~line 830). There are ~20 cwd-relative resolve('PRD.md')/resolve('plan') sites (system_context.md §2.2 lists all). The single-chdir strategy means NO per-call-site changes are needed — verify a representative sample.
2. INPUT: resolveRepositoryRoot + getInvocationCwd from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Add `--repo-root <path>` CLI flag in src/cli/index.ts on the root program option chain (near --prd at line 312). Add `repoRoot?: string` to both CLIArgs and ValidatedCLIArgs interfaces. In parseCLIArgs(), pass the parsed repoRoot through (it's a string path or undefined). In main(), if args.repoRoot is set, pass it as opts.explicit to resolveRepositoryRoot(INVOCATION_CWD, { explicit: args.repoRoot }) — the resolver resolves <path> against INVOCATION_CWD, then realpathSync + verify .git exists (dir or file), then the chdir uses that path. If <path> lacks .git, fail with the same NotARepositoryError. Enforce explicit-path semantics (§9.8.3): explicit --prd/--file/--session resolve against INVOCATION_CWD (they are passed to Commander which resolves relative to process.argv, but since chdir hasn't happened yet during parse, they resolve against the real invocation dir — CONFIRM this). Omitted/default paths (./PRD.md, ./plan/) resolve against the NEW process.cwd() (repo root) because they use bare resolve('PRD.md') which is cwd-relative AFTER chdir. Because the fix is a single bootstrap chdir, NO per-call-site changes are required at the ~20 resolve sites — add an integration test verifying resolve('PRD.md') from a subdir yields <repoRoot>/PRD.md. Check if PRPPipeline constructor (src/index.ts:245) passes repoRoot explicitly — if it does not (it passes args.prd which is already resolved), no change needed.
4. OUTPUT: --repo-root flag wired in src/cli/index.ts; repoRoot field in CLIArgs/ValidatedCLIArgs; explicit-vs-default path semantics verified via integration tests. Completes Task P1.M1.T1.
5. MOCKING: Use real temp git repos for integration tests. Mock is not needed for the flag parsing itself.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add --repo-root to the CLI reference in src/cli/index.ts option description (mirror §9.8.6 text). Update the main() comment to note --repo-root short-circuits the upward search.

tasks.title: Hard-error behavior, child-process inheritance, and acceptance verification
tasks.description: Verify that NotARepositoryError produces a single actionable exit-1 message before any session/agent work, that --help/--version work outside a repo, and that child processes inherit cwd=repoRoot. Add acceptance tests for all §9.8.9 criteria.

subtasks.title: No-repository hard error + child/agent inheritance + acceptance tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §2.1 and bootstrap-and-reporoot.md. The main().catch() handler at src/index.ts:~368 already handles typed errors (AuthPreflightError, HarnessProviderMismatchError, UnsupportedHarnessError) with clean console.error + process.exit(1). NotARepositoryError must be added as another arm of this catch handler. Child processes: src/agents/prp-executor.ts:550 uses cwd: process.cwd() — after chdir this is repoRoot. src/tools/git-mcp.ts:203 resolves path ?? process.cwd() — after chdir defaults to repoRoot.
2. INPUT: resolveRepositoryRoot, NotARepositoryError from P1.M1.T1.S1; --repo-root flag from P1.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: On NotARepositoryError, main() must abort with a single actionable message via the main().catch() handler (src/index.ts:~368): add `if (error instanceof NotARepositoryError) { console.error('\n❌ ' + error.message); process.exit(1); }`. The message must name the invocation directory searched from, the fact that no ancestor contains .git, and the --repo-root remediation. This MUST happen BEFORE creating any session, reading .hack/.env, or invoking any agent — verify by confirming the traversal runs before configureEnvironment() (line 128). Confirm --help/--version/invalid-flag still exit during parseCLIArgs() (they never reach the traversal — test `hack --help` from a non-repo dir exits 0). Verify child-process inheritance (§9.8.7): the parent chdirs before spawning bugfix children (task-orchestrator spawns) and agent subprocesses (prp-executor.ts:550) — they inherit cwd=repoRoot. Add tests covering ALL §9.8.9 acceptance criteria: (a) launched-from-subdir resolves repo root and process.cwd()===repoRoot; (b) worktree .git file detected correctly; (c) submodule resolves to submodule root; (d) no-repo exits 1 with no session created; (e) --help works outside any repo (exit 0); (f) --repo-root /explicit/path pins and skips search; (g) --repo-root with non-.git path errors; (h) explicit --prd ./relative resolves against invocation dir; (i) bare hack from subdir resolves default PRD.md to <repoRoot>/PRD.md.
4. OUTPUT: Hard-error path in main().catch(); child-process inheritance verified; comprehensive acceptance tests. Completes Milestone P1.M1 and Phase P1.
5. MOCKING: Mock process.cwd for no-repo tests. Use real temp git repos (incl. worktrees via `git worktree add`, submodules via `git submodule add`) for integration tests.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc on NotARepositoryError documenting the hard-error contract (exit 1, before any session/agent, actionable message per §9.8.5).

backlog.title: The .hack Configuration File — §9.7
backlog.description: A single TOML config file capturing every tunable default (§9.2.2 env-style settings and §5.3 CLI flags), with three-tier layering (global ~/.hack → project <repoRoot>/.hack → gitignored <repoRoot>/.hack.local), a secrets policy that keeps secrets out of version control, validation, and a hack config subcommand. This phase realizes the §9.2.1 7-layer precedence model and the env-over-file rule. Depends on Phase 1 (project layers are read from the resolved repo root).

milestones.title: TOML Loader, Three-Tier Layering, Secrets Policy & Validation
milestones.description: Add the TOML parser dependency, implement the parse module, build the three-tier discovery/merge loader with env-over-file seeding, and enforce the secrets policy + type/range validation with stderr-synchronous warnings/errors.

tasks.title: TOML parse, three-tier discovery/merge, and env-over-file seeding
tasks.description: Add the TOML parser dependency, create the parseHackFile function, implement the three-tier discovery/layered-merge loader that seeds process.env for unset keys, and wire it into main() after the Phase 1 chdir.

subtasks.title: TOML parser dependency + parse/validate module
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §3.1-§3.2 and config-system-and-constants.md. smol-toml@1.6.1 is ALREADY in node_modules as a transitive dep of markdownlint-cli but NOT in package.json dependencies. It must be promoted to a direct dependency: `"smol-toml": "^1.6.1"` in package.json dependencies. smol-toml exports `parse(string)` and `stringify(object)`, is ESM-native, TOML 1.0 compliant. It does NOT handle BOM — the loader must detect/reject a leading BOM manually (check first 3 bytes for 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF). All keys in .hack are lowercase snake_case per §9.7.4.
2. INPUT: None (foundational config module — no dependency on repo-root since the parse function takes an absolute path).
3. LOGIC: Add `smol-toml` to package.json dependencies (it's already installed). Create src/config/hack-config.ts with: (a) `parseHackFile(filePath: string): ParsedHackConfig` (§9.7.4): read file UTF-8, reject a leading BOM with a clear error (e.g. 'BOM detected in <file>; remove it and re-save as UTF-8 without BOM'), parse via `smol-toml.parse()`, catch parse errors and re-throw with file path + parser line/col, return a typed ParsedHackConfig object (a plain object keyed by [section] → key → value, with type info preserved). Define the ParsedHackConfig type and a HackConfigValue union (string | number | boolean). All keys are lowercase snake_case within their section (TOML tables map to [section]). The return type is `{ [section: string]: { [key: string]: HackConfigValue } }`.
4. OUTPUT: smol-toml in package.json dependencies; src/config/hack-config.ts with parseHackFile + ParsedHackConfig type. Consumed by P2.M1.T1.S2.
5. MOCKING: No external services to mock — TOML parsing is pure. Test with real TOML strings and temp files.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on parseHackFile documenting the format (TOML 1.0, UTF-8, BOM rejection), key casing (lowercase snake_case), and the return type. Note smol-toml as the parser dependency.

subtasks.title: Three-tier discovery, layered merge, env-over-file seeding
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §3.3. configureEnvironment() (src/config/environment.ts:62-114) reads process.env for ANTHROPIC_*, PRP_API_BASE_URL, etc. and writes ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Runtime getters (getResearchTimeoutSeconds(), etc.) read process.env lazily. The .hack loader must seed process.env ONLY for keys not already set (so shell env wins — env-over-file rule). Bootstrap: parseCLIArgs() → repo-root chdir (Phase 1) → .hack load → configureEnvironment() → pipeline. The insertion point in main() is between the chdir (P1.M1.T1.S1, after line 119) and configureEnvironment() (line 128). See §9.7.9 for ordering rationale.
2. INPUT: parseHackFile + ParsedHackConfig from P2.M1.T1.S1; getRepoRoot() from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement `loadHackConfig(repoRoot: string): MergedHackConfig` (§9.7.3) in src/config/hack-config.ts. Discover and parse THREE optional files in tier order: (1) Global: $HACK_CONFIG_HOME/config if set, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hack/config if set, else ~/.hack (use os.homedir()); (2) Project: <repoRoot>/.hack (committable); (3) Project-local: <repoRoot>/.hack.local (gitignored). Each higher tier overwrites the same key from a lower tier (per-section/key merge — nested object spread). A missing file at any tier is not an error (existsSync check → skip). Then seed process.env ONLY for keys not already set: for each merged key that maps to an env var (per the schema in P2.M2.T1.S1 — but for now, use a provisional mapping that covers all keys from §9.7.5 table), if process.env[ENV_VAR_NAME] is undefined, set process.env[ENV_VAR_NAME] = String(value). This realizes the env-over-file rule (§9.2.1 / §9.7.3): the merged file value is the default and real shell env / .env override it. For keys that map to CLI flags only (no env var), store them in the MergedHackConfig object for the CLI to read later (Phase 2.2). Wire the load into main(): call loadHackConfig(getRepoRoot()) AFTER the Phase 1 chdir and BEFORE configureEnvironment(). Define MergedHackConfig type extending ParsedHackConfig with a `_sources` metadata field tracking which tier each key came from (for --src in hack config show and for --log-level debug trace).
4. OUTPUT: loadHackConfig function + MergedHackConfig type; env seeding wired into main() bootstrap. Consumed by P2.M1.T2.S1 (secrets/validation) and P2.M2 (schema mapping + config subcommand).
5. MOCKING: Mock process.env via vitest vi.stubEnv. Use temp dirs for test .hack files.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on loadHackConfig documenting the tier order (global → project → project-local), env-over-file seeding rule ('seed process.env only for keys not already set'), and the §9.7.9 bootstrap position (after chdir, before configureEnvironment).

tasks.title: Secrets policy, validation, and error handling
tasks.description: Enforce the secrets refusal in committable .hack, implement type/range validation with warn-vs-hard-error semantics, ensure all warnings/errors go to stderr synchronously (§9.6), and add the effective-config debug trace.

subtasks.title: Secrets refusal + type/range validation + error semantics + debug trace
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §3.5 and config-system-and-constants.md §2. The existing deprecation-warning pattern in environment.ts uses synchronous console.warn (stderr, §9.6-compliant) with a module-private _deprecatedWarned Set for one-time dedup — mirror this pattern. The pino logger is configured AFTER config load (it needs --log-level which may come from .hack), so all config validation output must use console.warn/console.error to stderr. The secrets to refuse: [auth] override_key, [auth] zai_api_key, [auth] anthropic_api_key, [auth] anthropic_auth_token, or ANY key ending in _key/_token/_secret/_password. resolveApiKeyForProvider in harness.ts:57-80 reads PRP_API_KEY as the highest-priority credential override.
2. INPUT: loadHackConfig + MergedHackConfig from P2.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: In src/config/hack-config.ts, add a validation layer (called by loadHackConfig after parsing each tier, BEFORE env seeding): (a) SECRETS POLICY (§9.7.6): if any secret-bearing key is present in the COMMITTABLE project .hack (NOT .hack.local), emit a HARD error naming the file, offending key, and remediation (move to .hack.local or an env var), then abort (throw). .hack.local is the ONLY tier permitted to hold secrets; map [auth] override_key there to process.env.PRP_API_KEY during env seeding. Empty/whitespace-only secret values are treated as 'not configured' (never forwarded — §9.2.7 empty-string policy). (b) VALIDATION (§9.7.7): unknown section → warn once to stderr (console.warn) and continue (lenient, forward-compatible); unknown key in a known section → warn once with file/section/key and ignore (catch typos like reseaerch_depth); type mismatch or out-of-range value (e.g. [tasks_lock] poll_ms = -5, [harness] name = 'foo', [cli] mode = 'fast') → HARD error naming file, key, offending value, expected type/range, accepted values, abort (throw). (c) PARSE ERROR: already handled in parseHackFile — surface with file + line/col, abort. (d) DUPLICATE KEY: TOML itself rejects duplicates; smol-toml throws — surface verbatim with file path. All warnings/errors go to STDERR synchronously (console.warn for warnings, throw for hard errors — the main().catch() renders the thrown error). (e) EFFECTIVE-CONFIG TRACE: when --log-level debug is in effect (check process.env.HACKY_LOG_LEVEL or the parsed .hack [cli] log_level), log each key with its source layer (global/project/local/env/cli) and resolved value, MASKING secret values (e.g. 'override_key = "<redacted>"'). Note: this debug trace cannot use pino (logger not yet configured) — use console.warn to stderr.
4. OUTPUT: Secrets policy + validation functions in hack-config.ts; error semantics wired into loadHackConfig. Completes Milestone P2.M1.
5. MOCKING: Mock console.warn/console.error for warning capture. Use temp .hack files with deliberate secrets/errors/typos.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the validation/secrets functions documenting hard-error vs warn semantics (§9.7.7), the stderr requirement (§9.6/§9.7.7), the empty-string policy for secrets (§9.2.7), and the debug-trace masking.

milestones.description: Implement the exhaustive schema mapping connecting every [section].key to its env var and/or CLI flag, build the hack config subcommand (init/show/validate/path), manage .gitignore for .hack.local, and run full acceptance tests for §9.7.10.

tasks.title: Exhaustive schema mapping and canonical-name resolution
tasks.description: Implement the complete schema in hack-config.ts mapping every [section].key from §9.7.5 to exactly one env var and/or CLI flag, resolving the dual-config-surface ambiguities and handling bare-model-id qualification.

subtasks.title: Full schema map (all tunables) with env-var + CLI-flag seeding
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/config-system-and-constants.md §6-§7 for the COMPLETE CLI flag catalog and dual-config-surface map. Key findings: (a) RESEARCH_DEPTH has BOTH a constants.ts getter (getResearchDepth, L300) AND a CLI .default(process.env.RESEARCH_DEPTH ?? '2') — the TOML seeds the env var, CLI reads through it. (b) PARALLEL_RESEARCH is mentioned in --parallel-research description but NOT wired via .default() — isParallelResearch() reads process.env at runtime; the TOML key seeds PARALLEL_RESEARCH env var. (c) All HACKY_* env names (HACKY_LOG_LEVEL, HACKY_TASK_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS, HACKY_FLUSH_RETRIES, HACKY_PRP_CACHE_TTL, RESEARCH_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY, MONITOR_TASK_INTERVAL) live as inline string literals in src/cli/index.ts — promote to constants or reference by literal name in the schema. (d) [bug_hunt] results_file → BUG_RESULTS_FILE and [bug_hunt] fix_scope → BUGFIX_SCOPE are NOT in constants.ts — they are inline defaults. (e) [api] timeout_ms → API_TIMEOUT_MS is NOT currently defined anywhere. (f) qualifyModel() in environment.ts:159 is idempotent: 'glm-5.2' → 'zai/glm-5.2', 'zai/glm-5.2' → unchanged.
2. INPUT: MergedHackConfig + loadHackConfig from P2.M1.T1.S2; validation from P2.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement the exhaustive schema in src/config/hack-config.ts as a SCHEMA_MAP constant: an array of { section, key, envVar?, cliFlag?, type, defaultValue, acceptedValues? } entries, covering EVERY row of the §9.7.5 table. Sections: models, endpoint, harness, pipeline, commit, bug_hunt, validation, distributed_prd, tasks_lock, concurrency, api, monitor, cli, auth. Rules: (a) Each [section].key maps to EXACTLY ONE env var and/or CLI flag (no duplicate [cli]/[pipeline] pair for the same concept). (b) For dual concepts (RESEARCH_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY/--research-concurrency, HACKY_LOG_LEVEL/--log-level, MONITOR_TASK_INTERVAL/--monitor-task-interval, PARALLEL_RESEARCH/--parallel-research), the TOML key seeds the ENV VAR and the CLI option reads through it — only one TOML key per concept. (c) For booleans exposed as negating flags (--no-cache, --no-resource-monitor), the TOML key names the POSITIVE state (cache_enabled=true means cache is on; false means --no-cache). (d) Model-id values are written BARE (glm-5.2) and provider-qualified by the existing qualifyModel() path at read time (in environment.ts:159); already-qualified values (zai/glm-5.2) are accepted intact (qualifyModel is idempotent). The schema map drives: the env-seeding in loadHackConfig (provisional mapping becomes authoritative), the hack config show output (prints every key), and the validation (type/range checking). Add CLI-flag-only keys ([cli] mode, scope, max_tasks, max_duration_ms, continue_on_error, machine_readable, cache_enabled) to the MergedHackConfig — these seed the CLI default via process.env or a side channel, NOT directly overriding Commander defaults (Commander reads process.env in .default() for env-linked flags; for non-env-linked flags, the CLI layer must read the MergedHackConfig).
4. OUTPUT: SCHEMA_MAP constant in hack-config.ts; authoritative env-seeding via loadHackConfig. Consumed by P2.M2.T2 (config subcommand show/validate).
5. MOCKING: No external services to mock — schema is static data.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on SCHEMA_MAP cross-referencing the §9.7.5 table as the authoritative reference. Document the dual-surface resolution rule (one TOML key per concept, seeds env var, CLI reads through).

tasks.title: hack config subcommand (init / show / validate / path)
tasks.description: Add the `config` subcommand to src/cli/index.ts with four actions: init (writes commented template + .gitignore), show (prints effective config with --src and masked secrets), validate (CI-friendly lint), and path (prints resolved file paths).

subtasks.title: Register config subcommand + implement init/show/validate/path actions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/system_context.md §2.4 and bootstrap-and-reporoot.md §8. The `cache` subcommand (src/cli/index.ts:531-553) is the closest template: `program.command('cache').description(...).argument('[action]', ...).option(...).action(async (action, options) => { ... process.exit(0); })`. Command classes live in src/cli/commands/ (e.g. CacheCommand). The `config` subcommand should be registered in parseCLIArgs() alongside task/status/cache/inspect, and dispatched like the others (return { subcommand: 'config', options } sentinel). After Phase 1's chdir, resolve('plan')/resolve('PRD.md')/resolve('.hack') all resolve to repoRoot — the config subcommand benefits automatically. loadHackConfig(getRepoRoot()) provides the merged config; SCHEMA_MAP (P2.M2.T1.S1) provides the key list.
2. INPUT: SCHEMA_MAP + loadHackConfig from P2.M2.T1.S1; getRepoRoot from P1.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Create src/cli/commands/config.ts (a ConfigCommand class or plain functions). Register `config` subcommand in src/cli/index.ts mirroring the cache pattern: `program.command('config').description('.hack configuration file management').argument('[action]', 'Action: init, show, validate, path', 'show').option('--force', 'Overwrite existing .hack (init only)').option('--src', 'Annotate each value with its source layer (show only)').option('--global', 'Print global config path (path only)').option('--local', 'Print project-local config path (path only)').option('-o, --output <format>', 'Output format (table, json)', 'table').action(async (action, options) => { ... process.exit(0/1); })`. Add `{ subcommand: 'config'; options }` to the parseCLIArgs return union. Four actions: (a) INIT [--force]: write a heavily-commented <repoRoot>/.hack template (include all sections from SCHEMA_MAP as commented-out examples). Refuse to clobber existing .hack without --force. Append '.hack.local' to .gitignore (create .gitignore if absent — use fs.appendFileSync after checking if line already exists). Print next-step guidance. (b) SHOW [--src]: merge all layers (loadHackConfig + process.env + CLI args if available) and print every key from SCHEMA_MAP with its resolved value. MASK all secret values (keys ending _key/_token/_secret/_password → '<redacted>'). With --src, annotate each value with its winning layer (global/project/local/env/cli). Runs WITHOUT invoking any agent (safe for diagnosing auth/config). (c) VALIDATE [<file>]: lint .hack + .hack.local (or explicit file). Run the validation from P2.M1.T2.S1 on each. Exit 1 on errors, warn (stderr) on unknowns. CI-friendly. subtasks.title: Breakdown-in-progress detection + calm notice across all discovery-based actions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/009_94353b1a9fd3/architecture/session-and-tasks-json.md §3-§4 and system_context.md §4. The shared taskAction handler is at src/cli/index.ts:554-723. Tasks file resolution: --file override (line 580, explicit path) vs auto-discovery else-branch (lines 582-612: --session prefix match or findLatestSession, then findLatestBugfixTasksFile → main tasks.json fallback). The readFile call is at line 622 with NO existence check before it. sourceNote printing is at lines 614-620 (to stderr, suppressed for --output json). The catch block (lines 717-723) logs the error and exits 1 for ALL error conditions including ENOENT. findLatestSession (session-manager.ts:1573-1596) returns null when no sessions exist → the handler throws 'No sessions found...' at line 596. The session directory existing is the signal for breakdown-in-progress (SessionManager creates the dir + .prd_hash before tasks.json is written). This is INDEPENDENT of Phases 1-2 but benefits from Phase 1's repo-root chdir.
2. INPUT: None (independent of Phases 1-2; the taskAction handler already works, it just needs a pre-readFile existence check).
3. LOGIC: In src/cli/index.ts taskAction handler, AFTER the target session is resolved and the auto-discovered tasksFile is set (the ELSE branch of the --file/--session discovery — do NOT soften the explicit --file path at line 580) and BEFORE readFile(tasksFile) at line 622: insert an existence check. Use existsSync(tasksFile) (from node:fs — import existsSync alongside existsSync from the existing 'node:fs' import at the top of cli/index.ts). IF tasksFile does not exist AND the session directory DOES exist (existsSync(sessionPath)): classify the state as breakdown-in-progress (§5.3 Detection). Behavior: (a) SUPPRESS the sourceNote for this state (do not print 'Using main tasks: …' — it would be self-contradictory since the file doesn't exist). (b) If options.output === 'json': emit structured object to STDOUT: console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: 'awaiting_breakdown', session: '<session-id>' }, null, 2)). (c) Else: emit a single calm human-readable notice to STDERR (process.stderr.write): name the session and explain 'tasks.json is generated during PRD breakdown and is not available yet — re-run shortly, or run hack --continue to (re)generate it.' (d) Exit code 0 (process.exit(0)). (e) For the 'next' action under this state: the notice should say 'no tasks available yet (breakdown in progress)'. For JSON: { status: 'awaiting_breakdown', session: '<id>' }. LEAVE the existing 'No sessions found' path (findLatestSession returns null → throws at line 596) UNCHANGED — it still exits non-zero via the catch block, so the two empty states are distinguished. DO NOT trigger §5.1 corruption-recovery (keyed off present-but-broken file) or §4.4 interrupted-bugfix re-entry. Add tests: (1) hack status against session-without-tasks.json prints notice to stderr, exits 0, no ERROR/ENOENT/stack-trace on stdout; (2) --output json emits awaiting_breakdown object to stdout, exits 0; (3) --file /nonexistent still exits non-zero (explicit override not softened); (4) no-sessions-at-all still exits non-zero; (5) hack task and hack task next behave identically for the same state.
4. OUTPUT: Breakdown-in-progress handling across task/status/task next in src/cli/index.ts. Completes Milestone P3.M1 and Phase P3.
5. MOCKING: Use real temp session directories (create plan/NNN_hash/ dir with .prd_hash but no tasks.json). Mock SessionManager.findLatestSession for unit tests.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the breakdown-in-progress state and its exit code 0 in docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md (task/status section). Note that explicit --file and no-sessions paths remain hard errors.
